questions.q: The section **Intent Grounding Failure Modes and Their Checks** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: Phantom, stale, ambiguous, misclassified, and dynamically unreachable targets all arrive in the same well-formed wire format, so each needs its own detector.
An intent handoff must keep spatial containment, temporal freshness, dynamic effort, and a certified fallback, and the admission gates check them in cost order.
A target inside the static workspace is still inadmissible if the transit time at the speed ceiling exceeds the remaining evidence window (a handle 300 mm away needs 300 ms against a 219 ms horizon).
A grasp has force closure when its contacts can resist any external wrench within the friction cones, which bounds stability, not the magnitude of the squeeze.
